# discount_split

Spreads a discount over the lines of a bill in proportion to their amounts, a line at a time through the rule, so that the shares come to the discount

- File: `discount_split.kn` (module discount_split v1, sha256:3c55db386d63a643)
- Reads: the rule `discount_share` (`rules/discount_share.rule`)

## Functions

A function's effect puts it in one of three parts. A total function answers every input in the ranges it declares. A function checked when it runs has places the checks could not show: the generated code checks the value there, and when it is outside, fails with the kind of the place (`rule` and so on). A function that may not stop recurses.

### Total

#### `split`

Total: it answers every input in the ranges it declares. Its head writes `total`, and kaname holds it to that.

The running totals go to the rule; the last line carries what the rounding leaves.

```kn
fn split(lines: list[Line] count >=1 <=10, discount: money[USDc] range >=0USDc <=10_000_000USDc) -> list[Share] total
  description "The running totals go to the rule; the last line carries what the rounding leaves"
  map(running_totals(lines, l => l.amount), r =>
    Share { label: r.item.label, share: discount_share(discount: discount, before: r.before, upto: r.upto, total: r.total).share })
```

### Checked when they run

None.

None.

## Properties

A property claims that for every input in the ranges its parameters declare, and on which its `when` lines hold, its last line is `true`. `kaname check` tries it on the vectors and reports a counterexample as E603; it is shown only when `--lean` takes a proof of it. This page shows what each property says, not its answer.

### `every_line_keeps_its_label`

Each line gets one share, under its own label, in the order of the lines.

```kn
property every_line_keeps_its_label(lines: list[Line] count >=1 <=10, discount: money[USDc] range >=0USDc <=10_000_000USDc)
  description "Each line gets one share, under its own label, in the order of the lines"
  map(split(lines: lines, discount: discount), s => s.label) = map(lines, l => l.label)
```

It writes no `when` line: it holds for every input in the ranges. Its last line is `map(split(lines: lines, discount: discount), s => s.label) = map(lines, l => l.label)`.

The proof file `discount_split.lean` is beside the .kn; `ritsu check --lean` checks it.

### `shares_add_up`

The shares come to the discount: this rests on what the rule answers, which a proof knows only as far as the port says.

```kn
property shares_add_up(lines: list[Line] count >=1 <=10, discount: money[USDc] range >=0USDc <=10_000_000USDc)
  description "The shares come to the discount: this rests on what the rule answers, which a proof knows only as far as the port says"
  sum(split(lines: lines, discount: discount), s => s.share) = discount
```

It writes no `when` line: it holds for every input in the ranges. Its last line is `sum(split(lines: lines, discount: discount), s => s.share) = discount`.

The proof file `discount_split.lean` is beside the .kn; `ritsu check --lean` checks it.
